title: Retries & stopping rules
summary: Distinguish repeating an operation from correcting a result, and define when each must stop.

sections.label: Retry or correction
sections.text: A retry repeats an operation after a failure such as a connection problem. A correction uses findings to change an unacceptable result. An uncertain write outcome needs confirmation or reconciliation before another write.

sections.label: Proposed controls
items: Bound attempts, wall-clock time, tool calls, model calls, and spend.
Record why an attempt failed and what changed before retrying.
Stop repeated diagnosis that produces no new evidence.
Handle unavailable sources and permission denial as explicit outcomes.

sections.label: A bounded correction loop
sections.text: Specify which step receives the candidate and findings, what counts as an attempt and where the process stops. For example, two corrections after the initial candidate is a clear counting rule, not a recommended default. Recheck the revised result.

sections.label: Acceptance
sections.text: A run can end with a useful partial finding rather than fabricate completion. The reviewer can inspect attempted actions and remaining blockers.

sections.label: Gap review: workflow use and checks
items: Recommended use: Set bounded attempts and distinguish retries from corrections and uncertain completed writes.
Count attempts using an explicit rule and demonstrate the stopping outcome.
Replay a request after a simulated lost response and inspect the actual effect before retrying.
Workflow placement and checks are Atlas recommendations. Existing examples, tenant availability, older product claims and comparative benefits were not revalidated by this mapping review.

catalog.applicability: Use when defining how often an operation may be repeated or a result corrected, and what happens when the limit is reached. A retry repeats a failed operation, a correction changes an unacceptable result, and both need a counted limit and a stopping outcome.
catalog.limits: Reading a topic does not configure tools, execute a workflow or establish passing evidence.
